newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News-Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News-Feb 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which will see the doubling of the telecommunications industry in the next decade, nearly 70 nations have agreed to liberalise the A$800 billion global telecommunications market, ushering in competition, lowering consumer prices and boosting trade. The agreement prises open monopoly control of the telecommunications markets to foreign entry. Page 1.

Arnotts managing director Chris Roberts said yesterday that the extortion threat, which has resulted in the removal of biscuits from supermarket shelves in Queensland and New South Wales, may force the embattled company to stand down as many as 1,000 fulltime workers and cost the company as much as A$5 million a week in lost revenue.

Tasmanian Transport Minister John Cleary said yesterday that the Civil Aviation Safety Authority grounded air-ambulance service company, Airlines of Tasmania, and failed to notify the State Government. Cleary said he was disappointed that neither he nor the Department was notified of the suspension. Page 2.

The Australian Taxation Office hopes to net A$100 million per year from the fruit and vegetable industry which has become the next target for the ATO's reportable payments system. An information campaign on the system will begin today, ahead of a gradual phase-in process. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

An unprecedented wave of competition in phone service worldwide has been forecast after the agreement of nearly 70 countries to open up their telecommunications markets. The Geneva-based World Trade Organisation deal will allow the highly competitive teleommunications giants of the US and Europe to enter each others markets. Page 1.

Arnott's has begun laying off 1,000 workers across the country in the wake of extortion attempts against the company. Extortionists gave a deadline of today, saying that biscuits in Queensland and New South Wales would be poisoned unless four New South Wales police officers undergo public lie detector tests. Page 1.

The Federal Government is considering a proposal which would see parents' incomes means tested if their children living at home want to collect the dole. The plan aims to tighten eligibility for the dole for unemployed 16 to 20-year-olds to deter them from dropping out of study, and to make parents more accountable for their children. Page 1.

A vacant house behind the Turkish consulate in inner Sydney exploded into pieces shortly before 3 pm yesterday, possibly the result of a bomb, flattening the building. New South Wales police have not ruled out the possibility that the attack was politicaly motivated. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A former principal due to give evidence at the Police Royal Commission has committed suicide 24 hours before his court appearance. The principal had remained silent for 20 years about a teacher sexually abusing girls as young as 13 at his school, and had een stood down pending investigation into the matter. Page 1.

Australia's largest biscuit maker, Arnott's, may be forced to lay off a quarter of its staff following extortion attempts on their products. The company has removed biscuits from New South Wales and Queensland supermarkets on Friday. Page 1.

A vacant house in Woollahara was reduced to little more than rubble yesterday after a bomb blast at around 5 pm. The house was at the rear of the Turkish Consulate-General and police have not ruled out a political motive for the bombing. Police are searcing for a badly injured man seen staggering from the scene. Page 1.

The New South Wales Teachers Federation has banned all State-wide literacy and numeracy testing, angered over a proposal to use the test results in annual report cards on school performance, and amid fears the information will be used to rank schools base on the results. The move has blocked the State Government's election promise to give parents more information about the performance of individual schools. Page 1.
THE AGE

Government officials have confirmed that, over the weekend, 16 more cattle had died of the deadly anthrax disease and 12 more properties were found to be infected outside the five kilometre disease zone. A total of 105 cattle infected with the disease on 2 properties have been destroyed in attempts to halt the spread of the disease. Page 1.

Top medical researchers are urging Prime Minister John Howard not to bow to pressure from Independent MP Brian Harradine in deciding who will fill the position of chairman of the National Health and Medical Research Council. The researchers are concerned ederal Cabinet will veto the appointment of preferred candidate Professor John Funder from the Baker Medical Research Institute in Melbourne. Page 1.

The extortion attempt on Arnott's may see the company shed 1,000 jobs if the problem is not solved quickly. Biscuit stocks in Queensland and New South Wales supermarkets have been removed and a spokesman for the company said the threat could cost Arnotts $5 million a week in sales for as long as it continues. Page 1.

A revelation yesterday that the Federal Government was suppressing a report believed to have found no fault with the Civil Aviation Safety Board's competence has set back the Government's campaign against the CASA board. The report outlined an investigating in last year's crash of a Falcon Airline plane. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
